problems: BLOCKING: on author step curves (step, stepBefore, stepAfter, including the common `linkStyle default interpolate step`), a wide stroke of about 15 px or more puts the arrow tip about 20.5 px off the node border, up to 42 px. The head points sideways beside the node instead of into it. This happens in static scene() output, not only mid-drag. Over 30 random graphs where every edge has an author curve (stroke 12-30 px): 8 static, 12 routed and 718 frames in total with tips more than 1 px off. At 519b38c the same inputs have tips within 1.88 px, so this is a package regression. It is the same defect class as the r5 blocking item, which the lead requires to hold: tips on borders, and very wide strokes ending cleanly at the head.

Minimal reproductions (scratchpad verify/b1-arrows/r6): (a) min/m1.mmd = `flowchart TD; a[Alpha]-->b[Beta]; b-->c[Gamma]; a e1@--> c; e1@{ curve: step }; linkStyle 2 stroke-width:20px`. Moving Alpha by (-90,60) or Beta by (40,25) and calling route() or route_partial() puts the tip 20.5 px off; see png/m1_drag1.png (the head points right or left above Gamma, and covers Beta->Gamma's head). (b) genstep/s04.mmd, static: e7 n3->n5 (stepBefore, 16 px) tip at (221.5,405.5), scene end (207,420); see png/s04_side.png. (c) hand/h9_step_static.mmd, route() fed static centres: e3 a->d (step, 20 px) is 20.49 px off. (d) min/m4.mmd, `linkStyle default interpolate step`, is 20.54 px off mid-drag.

Root cause: curve_geometry (src/scene.rs:961-980) emits a trailing zero-length Seg::L whenever the last leg is axis-aligned. That covers Step with a vertical end leg, stepBefore with a vertical end leg, and stepAfter with a horizontal end leg, i.e. the usual TD/LR ends. square_end (src/scene.rs:1356) then finds no end heading and returns runs = INFINITY, so painted_trims never caps the cut. The full arrow_trim (the stroke width, about 20 px) wraps round the step's last corner when the real last leg is shorter. Routed stubs are 14.5 px, so the threshold is a stroke of about 15 px. The painted_trims doc comment itself names 'a step curve's short last leg' as a case that gets cut less, but the zero-length segment defeats it. Suggested fix: walk back past zero-length segments (or drop degenerate Seg::L in curve_geometry before squaring) and add step, stepBefore, stepAfter and interpolate-step cases to a_very_wide_strokes_head_keeps_its_tip_on_the_end_point, which currently covers no author step curve.

BLOCKING, same root cause: pick != render for that head's ink. Points inside the painted sideways head are missed by edge_at at tol 4, or pick the neighbouring edge: 112 random-probe mismatches on genstep/s04 (static and routed, e.g. (220.6,400.6) on e7 returns None), and 854 on hand/h9_step_static.

Same root cause at normal width, drag only: a 2 px step edge whose last axis-aligned leg falls below the 5.5 px cut mid-drag puts its tip 6.34 px off (genstep_w0/s?? e8 n3->n0, near frames; waypoints end (80.4,106.6)->(80.4,102.1)). Static and routed normal-width step curves were fine in every input I tried.

Everything else in the must-hold list checks out at d086bef, except the step-curve case above.

**Perf:** route_partial on bench-75 measured 5.47 and 6.81 ms max at HEAD vs 6.20 and 5.87 ms at 519b38c. It was already about 6 ms before the package and the means are close (3.2-3.5 vs 3.0-3.1 ms), so this is noise, not a regression. wide-labels drag_ms is bimodal on this box: HEAD 2.79-4.47 ms, 519b38c 2.84-4.04 ms, budget 3.89 ms; the minima are within budget.

**Non-blocking polish:**
- A 55 px stroke gets an arrow-t48 head, because the trim is clamped at 48. Its butt sits 3.5 px outside the head in static output (gen/g7_05, gen/g7_32).
- One thick start head is capped to a 0.8 px cut, leaving its butt 1.35 px outside the head (static, gen/g7 random set, n5->F0).
- The straight end stub adds a few new sharp corners to the static spline waypoints (bench-75 108->111, dense-lr 46->48). These are spline control points the painter also uses, so hosts stay consistent.
- The README now says a wide line's head has 'its tip on the node border'. That is not true for step curves until the blocking item is fixed.
